questions.stem: For delta H = +40 kJ/mol, delta S = +100 J/mol K, is reaction spontaneous at 300 K?
questions.explanation: Delta G = 40 - 300*0.1 = 40 - 30 = +10 kJ/mol, positive, so not spontaneous at 300 K. Threshold is 400 K.

questions.topic: Equilibrium constant from standard Gibbs energy
questions.learningObjective: Compute K at different temperature
questions.stem: Given delta H = -50 kJ/mol, delta S = -100 J/mol K, estimate K at 500 K.
questions.explanation: At 500 K, delta G = -50 - 500*(-0.1) = 0, so K = exp(0) = 1. This is the crossover temperature.

questions.topic: Le Chatelier response to compression
questions.learningObjective: Predict shift when removing product
questions.stem: Removing a product from a gaseous equilibrium shifts equilibrium toward?
questions.explanation: Removing product disturbs equilibrium; system produces more product to replace it. Shift is toward products.

questions.topic: Converting a pressure constant to a concentration constant
questions.learningObjective: Compute delta n from balanced equation
questions.stem: For reaction 2A(g)+B(g)->3C(g), find delta n of gas.
questions.explanation: Delta n = moles gaseous products - reactants = 3 - (2+1) = 0. Thus Kp = Kc for this reaction.

questions.topic: Equilibrium extent of a reaction solved by bisection
questions.learningObjective: Explain why bisection needs a sign change
questions.stem: Explain why bisection requires the function to change sign over the interval.

answer.exemplar: By the intermediate value theorem, a continuous function changing sign must have a root in the interval.

questions.explanation: Bisection relies on the intermediate value theorem. A continuous function with opposite signs at endpoints must cross zero somewhere inside.
